added: Delete a list from the editor's ⋯ menu, instead of leaving it to find the list on another page.
Forget a list from the editor's ⋯ menu: it leaves this device but stays online for anyone holding its link.
When a saved list can’t be opened anymore, the page names it and lets you forget it.
Food and fuel picked from the catalog arrive marked consumable, so a Clif bar never counts toward base weight.
My Gear now remembers the calories you've entered for a food, and brings them back the next time you add it to a list.
The sharing panel says when a list was opened from your account rather than its edit link, and can hand this device a fresh one.
changed: Switching between the gear, packing and planning views is instant on a long list.
Delete list in the editor's ⋯ menu reads in red.
Each action in the editor's ⋯ menu now carries an icon, so the menu can be scanned by shape as well as read.
Your gear vault is now called My Gear, everywhere it's named.
"Your lists" is no longer a page. Your lists live in the editor's switcher, and forgetting or deleting one is in its ⋯ menu.
When a list's gear already reaches My Gear on its own, each row's save button reads "Already in My Gear" and goes quiet.
The consumable and worn toggles swapped places, and a water row carries a lit consumable mark, so the marks line up in one column.
When a list's gear already reaches My Gear on its own, each row's save button steps aside instead of sitting dimmed.
The save button sits first in a row's trailing icons, so the icons every row shares hold a steady column.
A new row offers Save to My Gear once it has a name and a weight or a catalog pick, not before.
Coming back to the planning view is instant, and it keeps where you left it.
A shared list's heading is tighter: who made it and when on one line, the trail and the dates on the next.
A shared list no longer labels itself "Read-only". There was never anything on the page to edit.
On a wide screen, an item's quantity has a + and a − beside the number. On a phone it stays a plain field.
The packs button's corners now match the Gear / Packing / Planning switcher it sits above.
fixed: A pack whose edit link was replaced no longer shows up twice in the list switcher.
Forgetting or deleting a list now sticks. It no longer turns up again in the list switcher.
Renaming a list shows in the list switcher straight away.
The browser tab shows a list's new name the moment you refresh, instead of the name it was carrying a minute ago.
Renaming a row to a different piece of gear no longer leaves the old product's catalog weight behind.
Typing a list's name while the list is still loading no longer loses the start of it.
Correcting a piece of gear's spelling or product link reaches My Gear straight away.
A list that can't reach the server says "Not saved" and holds still while it retries, with a growing pause.
The editor's toolbar icons sit at the right edge again on a list that hasn't been edited yet.
Forgetting a list that’s no longer online warns that this device's copy may be all that’s left.
Water rows no longer offer Save to My Gear. Water is a volume you carry, not gear.
On a phone, packing mode no longer shows each item twice.
Typing "water" and tapping away marks the row consumable, the same as choosing the water suggestion.
A list made while signed in shows up in the list switcher on your other devices, and opens there from the account, no edit link needed.
The Worn and Consumable switches read clearly when they're off, in dark mode too.
The Worn and Consumable switches are a full-size tap target; they look the same.
Saying "click Consumable" to a speech-input tool finds the Consumable switch.
A row's ⋯ menu opens upward when the row sits near the bottom of the screen.
"New list" in the pack switcher now lights up under the pointer and the keyboard, like the lists above it.
On a water row the weight's unit now lines up with every other row's instead of sitting slightly right of the column.
Adding an item near the bottom of the page scrolls just far enough to show the new row.
The unit menu on a folder's last item no longer gets cut off at the folder's edge.
